transcript.title: Opening
transcript.text: Good morning Rushil Bhatia. Here is your daily news for Sunday, November 1. In today's briefing: top headlines, bhopal and madhya pradesh, business and markets, money, tax and personal finance, science and technology, development and policy, across india, around the world. Let's begin.

transcript.title: Top headlines
transcript.text: First, the stories leading the news this morning. 23 years later: Pakistan recreate India's Lord's magic with record-equalling chase. Pakistan produced a memorable run chase to beat Sri Lanka by three wickets in the One-Day International tri-series final in Lahore on Saturday. Fakhar Zaman led the charge with a brilliant century as the hosts chased down a target of 326 with nine balls to spare. Pakistan finished on 331 for seven in 48.3 overs to register the joint-highest successful chase in an ODI final. Pakistan equalled India's famous record against England in the 2002 NatWest Series final at Lord's. Island nation's treaty with Australia raises concerns over loss of cultural heritage. Tuvalu's recent treaty with Australia allows its citizens to migrate for work and study opportunities abroad. While migration offers new options, concerns exist regarding the preservation of cultural heritage. Traditional buildings and construction skills might be at risk as populations shift. Researchers are documenting Tuvalu's architectural history through photographs and digital models. Pilibhit voter roll row: UP CEO orders statewide ECINET login shutdown. Uttar Pradesh Chief Electoral Officer Navdeep Rinwa has taken stringent action against voter registration irregularities. He ordered the deactivation of login IDs used by voter registration centre operators. Following an inquiry, an outsourced computer assistant was terminated for their alleged involvement. District election officers have been instructed to verify the deactivation of these IDs promptly. Armless archer Sheetal Devi wins double gold at Asian Para Games. Sheetal Devi, born without arms, has developed a unique technique for archery using her feet, shoulder, and mouth. She was introduced to sports by the Indian Army and trained under Coach Kuldeep Vedwan. At the 2026 Asian Para Games, she won two gold medals and one silver, defending her previous titles successfully. Her achievements inspire children with disabilities to pursue sports and contribute positively to their lives. 10L turnout target, 4,000 cops, 200 CCTV: Delhi braces for INDIA bloc's anti-CEC rally. Delhi is gearing up for INDIA bloc rally at Ramlila Maidan on Sunday, with opposition parties expecting a turnout of up to 10 lakh people and police deploying more than 4,000 personnel to manage security and crowds. Glenn Phillips on the brink of breaking world record versus India. Phillips has scored 276 runs in the ongoing series. His tally includes the 107 he made off 49 balls in the fourth T20I on Friday (October 30). He needs another 56 runs in the final match to break the all-time record. 6.0-magnitude earthquake strikes Japan's coast near Shima. 15 UTC (3:45 am IST) on Saturday. 4.1bn-year-old pink Mars rock found in Sahara holds clues to ancient water. Discovered in the vast Sahara Desert, the meteorite Teghaza 001 is over four billion years old and is confirmed to be a Martian rock via isotopic studies. This intriguing specimen reveals a volcanic history intertwined with water activity, indicating a complex water cycle on Mars. As researchers delve deeper into its origins, they are unraveling vital insights into the planet's early environmental conditions. 'Politicisation of energy flows harmful': EAM calls for diversified supply chains at G20. External affairs minister S Jaishankar on Saturday called for reducing political interference in energy markets and diversifying global supply chains, saying disruptions were placing a disproportionate burden on developing countries. Man rescued a 2kg bear cub; the 150kg bear still tries to sit on his lap. In 2019, electrician Petar Tubic stumbled upon a deserted bear cub named Masa in the woods. Over time, he nurtured Masa, eventually establishing a sanctuary for rescued animals, which now includes an additional bear, Ljubica. However, Tubic is troubled by their strong human bonds, raising concern over the bears' future. The sanctuary has transformed into a community attraction and draws attention to the complexities involved in wildlife rescue. Authoritarianism sets in when society fears questions: Justice Bhuyan. At a time when the opposition has branded the NDA govt authoritarian, Justice Ujjal Bhuyan Saturday said authoritarianism sets in when society fears questions, and stressed people must shed the binary of 'us' and 'they' and adopt the core constitutional philosophy of 'we' to preserve the country's unity in diversity. Trump says Brazil's Bolsonaro can stay in US 'as long as he wants'. Recently, Donald Trump hinted at the possibility of Flavio Bolsonaro remaining in the U.S. indefinitely after his election loss. Amid looming legal challenges and safety fears, he orchestrated a dramatic escape featuring false vehicles and chartered jets. Trump's backing of their humanitarian parole status illuminates the stark political unrest and ongoing controversies surrounding Bolsonaro in Brazil.
